subject.title: [Feature]: First-class org/team deployment — workspace scaffolding, RBAC, and deployment manifests

question: Which parts of first-class org/team deployment should OpenClaw core own now, and what tenant/session/tool-policy security boundary is approved for the first implementation?
rationale: The requested CLI scaffold, deployment manifest, and RBAC model would define new public product and security contracts across config, Gateway auth, sessions, tool policy, and docs, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent boundary.

options.title: Decompose Under This Umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open and approve narrow sub-issues only after threat-model, config, and upgrade contracts are explicit.

options.title: Keep Strong Isolation External
options.body: Keep core focused on missing auth/session/tool-policy APIs while scaffolding and manifests live in plugins, docs, or external deployment tooling.

options.title: Decline First-Class Team Mode
options.body: Close the umbrella after documenting separate Gateways, trusted proxy, and per-agent profiles as the supported isolation pattern.

recommendation.title: Decompose Under This Umbrella
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and approve narrow sub-issues only after threat-model, config, and upgrade contracts are explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest verified history signal across the trust-model docs and Gateway identity/auth surfaces that frame this decision.
